{{Quote|We are always eager to take advantage of shifting political realities.|Presidente Shu Mai|<ref name="S&V WOB">{{StarshipsVehiclesCite|77|Welcome On Board}}</ref>}}
The '''Commerce Guild''' was a trade conglomerate made up of major commercial entities, such as the [[SoroSuub Corporation/Legends|SoroSuub Corporation]]. The Guild was known for pressuring smaller companies to join.

The Commerce Guild was dissolved following the [[Mission to Mustafar/Legends|execution]] of [[Presidente/Legends|Presidente]] [[Shu Mai/Legends|Shu Mai]] and was [[Imperialization/Legends|absorbed]] by the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]].

==History==
The guild went as far back as [[700 BBY]], when it maintained a [[Commerce Guild trading station|trading station]] in the [[Bpfassh system/Legends|Bpfassh system]].
Companies that resisted the Guild were placed under tremendous pressure by the Guild, including its security forces. Like the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]], [[Corporate Alliance/Legends|Corporate Alliance]] and the [[InterGalactic Banking Clan/Legends|InterGalactic Banking Clan]], the Commerce Guild had its own [[Commerce Guild Punitive Security Forces/Legends|security forces]]. The Guild was also politically powerful as it was economic and had several corrupt [[Planet/Legends|planetary]] officials, [[Senator/Legends|senators]], and industrial spies in its fold.

[[File:Shu_Sullust.jpg|thumb|left|175px|[[Shu Mai/Legends|Shu Mai]] and members of the Guild on [[Bassadro]].]]

The Commerce Guild also had the power to buy entire planets. One such planet was [[Castell/Legends|Castell]], the homeworld of the [[Gossam/Legends|Gossam]]. The Commerce Guild enslaved the entire population of Castell. At the time, [[Shu Mai/Legends|Shu Mai]] was the Commerce Guild's [[Chief of Property Resources]]. She initially used her position to liberate her people, but then followed this by raising the required tribute from her fellow Gossam. The Commerce Guild Chief of Staff was so pleased with Mai that they gave her the office of [[Presidente/Legends|Presidente]] of the Commerce Guild.<ref name="GPB">{{GamerCite|10|Galactic Power Brokers}}</ref> Afterward, Mai negotiated aggressively and managed to end the financial crisis that had ravaged Castell for a decade. The planet then gained importance for the Guild as a manufacturing center.<ref name="UAA">''[[Ultimate Alien Anthology]]''</ref>

In [[27 BBY/Legends|27 BBY]], the Commerce Guild introduced a bill for [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]] approval, one that would give the Guild a ''de facto'' monopoly over banking practices in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]]. To improve the possibilities of its adoption, the Guild bribed several voting Senators to sponsor it. Many others, including Senator [[Bail Prestor Organa/Legends|Bail Prestor Organa]] of [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaan]], openly opposed it, even swearing to stop the legislative motion. To get rid of the Senatorial opposition's interference, the Guild arranged to incriminate the Senators, tarnish their reputations, and possibly ruin their careers, by using their names in ''falsified betting'' on various events and by rigging an accident at an "illegal" podrace during the [[Galactic Games/Legends|Galactic Games]] of [[26 BBY/Legends|26 BBY]] on [[Euceron]]. The Guild's plot would have a podracer collide into the spectator-filled grandstands, taking many lives, and leaving the Senators to blame. [[Liviani Sarno]], a member of the Guild and head of the [[Games Council]], organized the conspiracy with the help of [[Maxo Vista]], who desired Guild membership. The plot was discovered by [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] and [[Jocasta Nu/Legends|Jocasta Nu]], and stopped by [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]]. As Organa and the rest of the opposition were left still standing, politically (the falsified betting having been uncovered), the law was vetoed.<ref name="JQ3">''[[Jedi Quest: The Dangerous Games]]''</ref>

Nevertheless, the guilty parties were not brought to justice,<ref name="JQ3" /> thanks, in large measure, to the perjury of the power-hungry [[Bog Divinian]], a Games Council member who wanted the Guild to be indebted to him&mdash;something he achieved. With the help of the Guild and other sponsors, Divinian obtained political power by being elected to the Galactic Senate, and thus retained the sympathies of the Guild. However, Divinian's career was soon forfeit, with the debacle that became the [[24 BBY/Legends|24 BBY]] [[Anti-Jedi sentiment/Legends|anti-Jedi]] factional petition to sever all future Jedi affiliation with the Senate. The petition failed miserably, accompanied as it was by a [[Attack on the Senate Building|vicious attack]] by two of the galaxy's greatest criminal minds upon that august body, assembled as it was in full-body session in the [[Grand Convocation Chamber|Senate Rotunda]] to debate the petition. With that unmitigated failure and near-catastrophe (the Jedi having ultimately foiled the attack), the Guild lost all interest in further helping Divinian.<ref name="JQ9">''[[Jedi Quest: The False Peace]]''</ref>

In [[25 BBY/Legends|25 BBY]], the criminal [[Slams|Slam gang]] attempted to break into a security vault of the Commerce Guild. Before they could perform their heist, the Slams were captured and sent to prison.<ref name="JQ8">''[[Jedi Quest: The Changing of the Guard]]''</ref>

In [[24 BBY/Legends|24 BBY]], the Commerce Guild opened an office on the tax-free world of [[Korriban/Legends|Korriban]]. Guild members deserving a punishment were sent there, although the Guild motivated other corporations to open offices in the Korriban spaceport of [[Dreshdae]]. By [[23 BBY/Legends|23 BBY]], local Guild executives were being robbed in their hotels with alarming frequency. Using local crime against Guild workers as an excuse, the Guild sent a droid army (including [[DSD1 dwarf spider droid/Legends|dwarf spider droids]] and [[OG-9 homing spider droid/Legends|homing spider droids]]) to Korriban, violating [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Republic]] laws. This likely was the beginning of the corroborative relationship of Shu Mai and [[Count/Legends|Count]] [[Dooku/Legends|Dooku]], for some of these droids, as well as new Republic regulation-violating [[B2-series super battle droid/Legends|super battle droids]], were employed by Dooku's alter-ego [[Dooku/Legends|Darth Tyranus]] in fending off [[Mission to Korriban (23 BBY)|Jedi intrusion]] into the long-abandoned [[Great Temple (Korriban)|Great Temple]] and [[Sith Academy (Korriban)|Sith Academy]], where he had set up a base for rendezvousing with galactic criminals [[Granta Omega]] and [[Jenna Zan Arbor]], to establish an alliance with them.<ref name="JQ10" />

In the years leading up to the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], Shu Mai greatly increased the military and commercial clout of the Guild. She also instigated strife on [[Ansion/Legends|Ansion]], resulting in the [[Border dispute on Ansion/Legends|Mission to Ansion]], and aligned the Guild with Count Dooku's [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Separatist movement]].

In [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]], Mai was present in a meeting of Separatist leaders on [[Geonosis/Legends|Geonosis]] which saw the birth of the Confederacy of Independent Systems. She knew that support of the Separatists would be [[Treason/Legends|treason]] against the Galactic Republic, but she could not resist the lure of promised wealth. She allied the Commerce Guild with the Confederacy during the Clone Wars, and supplied armies of [[Battle droid/Legends|battle droids]] to their [[Separatist Droid Army/Legends|Droid Army]] and [[Starship/Legends|starships]] to their [[Confederate Navy/Legends|starfleet]].

During the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], [[Shu Mai/Legends|Shu Mai]] attempted to use combined military might from both the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]] and Commerce Guild to distribute deadly [[trihexalon]] on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] and therefore eliminate the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Republic Senate]]. The plot was prevented by a group of [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] padawans led by [[Mavra Zane]] and [[Chewbacca/Legends|Chewbacca]].

Following the execution of Shu Mai at [[Mustafar/Legends|Mustafar]] by [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]] in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]], the Commerce Guild ceased to exist, and its remaining holdings were absorbed by the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]]. Despite the Guild's dissolution , a few of it's subsidiaries such as SoroSub and the Mining Guild were allowed to survive and continued to thrive into the Imperial Era due to the Empire becoming their largest customer.  <ref name="TNEGtD" /> At least one Commerce Guild employee, [[Iaco Stark/Legends|Iaco Stark]], took refuge within the [[Corporate Sector Authority/Legends|Corporate Sector Authority]].
